examples.enunciado: How do TCP and UDP differ in the way that they establish a connection between two endpoints?
alternativas: TCP uses the three-way handshake, and UDP does not guarantee message delivery.
TCP uses synchronization packets, and UDP uses acknowledgment packets.
UDP provides reliable message transfer, and TCP is a connectionless protocol.
UDP uses SYN, SYN ACK, and FIN bits in the frame header while TCP uses SYN, SYN ACK, and ACK bits.
examples.explicacao_profunda: TCP is connection-oriented: before data transfer it completes a three-way handshake (SYN → SYN-ACK → ACK) so both endpoints agree on sequence numbers and readiness. UDP is connectionless and sends datagrams without a setup phase or delivery guarantee. Option B is incomplete and misleading — UDP does not use ACK packets for transport reliability. Option C reverses the roles: UDP is unreliable/connectionless; TCP is reliable/connection-oriented. Option D confuses layers and protocols: SYN/FIN/ACK are TCP segment flags in the transport header, not UDP frame bits, and UDP does not implement that handshake.

examples.enunciado: In which way does a spine-and-leaf architecture allow for scalability in a network when additional access ports are required?
alternativas: A spine switch and a leaf switch can be added with redundant connections between them.
A spine switch can be added with at least 40 GB uplinks.
A leaf switch can be added with connections to every spine switch.
A leaf switch can be added with a single connection to a core spine switch.
examples.explicacao_profunda: In a spine-and-leaf fabric, every leaf connects to every spine. To add access ports you deploy a new leaf and uplink it to all spines, preserving equal-cost multipath and predictable east-west latency. Adding only a spine does not by itself create new access ports for endpoints. A single uplink from leaf to one spine breaks the full-mesh leaf-to-spine design and creates a bottleneck/single path. Fixed uplink speeds (e.g. 40 Gbps) are a capacity choice, not the scalability mechanism when you need more edge ports.
